answer: Agents anchor their existence by performing 7,000,000 sequential operations, a temporal gate that mandates strictly linear execution to prevent parallel shortcuts. An honest participant pays this cost once, while 1,000 fakes must incur 7,000,000,000 cycles to bypass the verifier. A node acts as a vault for incoming execution logs, checking each against a comet trajectory of expected state transitions, while a timber analyzer audits the serialized output for integrity. We assume single-core silicon depth is fixed.
